text: Understanding Git branching is essential for effective version control. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to develop and test their changes safely. Once the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the code and suggest improvements. This workflow keeps the project organized and reduces the risk of errors. By using feature branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can collaborate smoothly and maintain a clean, reliable codebase.
